title: PreferenceNoiseSim: A Simulation Tool for Measuring Reward Model Robustness to Label Noise

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Understanding which noise types damage reward models most helps prioritize annotation QA. Impact is practical but moderate; the finding is about data quality rather than a fundamental safety mechanism.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Applying controlled noise perturbations to HH-RLHF is straightforward, but training multiple small reward models under each noise condition requires significant ML engineering. Multiple training runs add compute and complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple noise conditions, multiple reward model training runs, evaluation on RewardBench, and producing noise robustness curves. The combinatorial experiment design is too broad for 30 hours at beginner level.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
